o: Implement partial application: bind args to fn, leaving '_' holes. When the returned function is called with restArgs, fill holes left-to-right from restArgs, then append leftovers. Examples show no-hole appending ([2,4,6]+[8,10]) and hole filling ([1,2,'_',4,'_',6] with [3,5] → [1,2,3,4,5,6]).
k: Fill placeholders in order, then append unused restArgs at the end.

a.i: Clone args, walk it replacing '_' with successive restArgs values, push the remainder, then invoke fn with spread/apply.
s: Clone args into a working array.
Replace each '_' with the next unconsumed restArgs element.
Call fn with the working array as individual arguments.
a.sp: O(args.length + restArgs.length) for the merged copy

w: On LeetCode this is JavaScript-only; the JS version above is the canonical submission. Pitfall: stop filling once restArgs is exhausted (guaranteed not to happen here, but defensive coding is good), and remember leftovers go AFTER filled args, not into remaining holes.
